source: Windows CI run 45159836136 (phase 1 at 1039b44, PR merge commit b6e98fc): every suite present then produced exactly these outcomes on Windows. Added after 1039b44 and so far recorded on macOS only: test_app_paths.py, test_host.py, test_host_imports.py, test_window_layout.py, test_file_io.py, test_launcher_discovery.py, test_game_target.cjs, test_mac_task_tiers.cjs and the selector test in test_windows_contract.cjs; HostImportTests.test_win32_overlay_backend_imports is skipped off Windows and recorded with its Windows outcome (pass in runs on 06c9c07 and 00d5531), so a Windows-only regression there cannot hide behind a skip. Refresh from the offline-test-results artifact when Windows outcomes change.

the Windows contract: empty tiers mark nothing
a manifest error alone marks nothing and keeps the error
macOS marks verified, experimental and excluded entries from the shipped manifest
malformed backend values are dropped, not trusted
macOS starts wait for the tiers and stop on a manifest error; other systems never wait
an empty or malformed macOS tier response is a load error that refuses starts
a scheduled slot waits for a delayed tier response instead of being refused
the scheduler never waits off macOS: the slot starts before a teardown, as before
a scheduler stopped while waiting for the Mac tiers records nothing and a later start still runs the slot
a scheduler restarted while waiting for the Mac tiers runs the due slot once with the new handler
a scheduler waiting for the Mac tiers starts the slot once they arrive
macos names the mailbox correctly when the launch task before it was refused
macos registers no names rather than guessing by position without the mapping
windows pairs returned IDs with submitted tasks by position
